source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Boot into OS
2. Check driver/firmware version.
3. Update driver and firmware
4. Restart OS

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Check the Driver and Firmware are latest and match update file.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: vendor RAID update tool + driver/FW package (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Generic `storcli /c0 download fw=${RAID_FW_IMAGE}` example followed by version checks.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; notes the package and flash risk but assumes `/c0` and does not validate the linked Linux script or kernel/module compatibility.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; adds controller identity, script revision, package hash, kernel support, recovery and complete storage evidence.

original_test_intent: On Linux, update the approved RAID driver and controller firmware, restart the OS, and verify the same controller reports the project-approved versions while its virtual disks and host storage remain healthy.
original_method: Inventory PCI/controller identity, kernel/module and firmware; review and pin the referenced script plus signed package hashes; execute the approved driver and firmware stages in vendor order; rebuild initramfs only if documented; restart; then verify versions, module binding, arrays, boot and logs.
manual_activity: One authorized user must approve the exact controller, script/package set and recovery plan. The Linux update, restart, health monitoring and evidence capture do not intrinsically require physical or visual work, so approval/package availability do not make it partial.
required_inputs: Controller model/serial/PCI path, boot/data role and current PD/VD state
Linux distribution, kernel and current/target module versions
Immutable referenced-script revision and code review result
Signed driver/firmware packages, hashes and compatibility matrix
Maintenance approval, stable power, OOB and vendor recovery path
safety_requirements: Resolve the exact controller; never default to `/c0` or update all adapters.
Inspect the linked script for target selection, shell safety, hidden retry and destructive side effects before use.
Do not unload a module serving root or active data outside an explicit vendor-supported plan.
Require healthy arrays/no rebuild and verified package compatibility before flashing; maintain stable power.
Do not auto-retry, roll back, switch packages or repeat reboot after failure; preserve first-failure evidence.
agent_execution_scope: Collect pre-state controller/PCI/kernel/module/VD/boot evidence and validate script/package gates.
Execute only the reviewed approved script or documented vendor commands for the bound target.
Track return codes and required initramfs/restart stages, then verify same-device binding and versions.
Collect journal/kernel/controller/BMC health and report Tool Result separately from verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the controller, exact script revision/packages and maintenance/recovery plan.
Define project-approved target versions and acceptable log exceptions.
Evaluate post-update evidence and decide PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not safe to execute generically: it assumes controller 0, lacks driver/module handling, ignores the linked script revision and supplies no compatibility proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Prefer the reviewed source-linked project script when it matches the detected controller/kernel; otherwise use only documented vendor Linux commands for the approved versions.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Linux driver and firmware update, restart, source script, log review and 5/10-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Pin the project script and packages by digest, bind the controller by serial/PCI identity, validate kernel/module compatibility, and gate pre-update, update, restart and post-health phases.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact Linux/kernel, RAID adapter/firmware and boot topology.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record script commit, package hashes, kernel, module, firmware, vendor utility and BIOS/BMC.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Controller vendor Linux driver/firmware/recovery documentation and project script revision.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds supply-chain, target and boot-module controls without replacing either update.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Reviewed script and vendor compatibility evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A successful flash code cannot prove initramfs, driver binding or virtual disks survived restart.

project_override_considerations: A qualified project baseline may differ from the newest vendor release. Claims must name the exact approved driver and firmware, script revision and affected controller only.
expected_evidence: Controller/PCI/serial, kernel/module, firmware, PD/VD/boot pre-state and package/script hashes
Full script/vendor-tool transcript with exact target, return codes and initramfs/reboot actions
Post-restart kernel/module binding and controller firmware versions matching the manifest
VD/PD/boot health, journal/dmesg/syslog and BMC/SEL comparison, Tool Result and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure and criterion align on updating and verifying both components. The meaning of `latest` is missing but can be supplied as a project version baseline.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The common case awaits platform packages and approval but has clear semantics and a fully automatable path once ready.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps the flash-risk warning while rejecting its controller assumption and missing Linux driver path.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains identity, kernel, script and recovery controls but changes the class because governance does not itself require manual execution.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Treats the linked script as a versioned artifact requiring review and separates machine result from engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Protects boot-critical Linux storage from generic flashing while allowing an approved workflow to remain correctly classified as automatable.
independent_technical_reasoning: Every core action exposes a scriptable Linux/vendor interface, including restart and structured verification. Risk mandates gates and no retry, but no human physical setup or observation is required by the source.

source_provenance.history: Exact-code repository search including source script URL

no_automatic_retry: Do not re-run the script, flash, rebuild initramfs, unload modules or reboot again after failure. Preserve state and escalate.
